sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Short-Acting Reversible Hormonal Methods of Contraception
sources.text: Additionally, the nurse will use the MEC Criteria (see 5.1 Contraception: The Nurse’s Role to ensure the person has no contraindications to combination hormonal birth control. The nurse will then educate the person on how and when to start COCs ( Table 5.7 ). (attribution: Copyright Rice University, OpenStax, under CC BY NC-SA 4.0 license) Risks and Side Effects of the Transdermal Patch The contraceptive patch has the same mechanism of action, side effects, risk factors, and MEC criteria as all other combined hormonal contraception. The patch should not be used in persons weighing more than 198 pounds (90 kilograms) as it is not as effective ( Birth control patch , 2023). The contraceptive ring has the same mechanism of action, side effects, risk factors, and MEC criteria as all other combined hormonal contraception, with the addition of vaginitis as a side effect. sources.name: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Pain Assessment
sources.text: This scale has five criteria: face, legs, activity, cry, and consolability. Based on their observations of the patient, the provider assigns each of the five criteria a score of 0, 1, or 2. The provider then adds the scores of each of the five criteria to calculate the overall pain score. The overall total will be between 0 and 10, with 0 being no pain and 10 being severe pain. This scale has five criteria: breathing independent of vocalization, negative vocalization, facial expression, body language, and consolability. Similar to the FLACC scale, each of the five criteria in the PAINAD scale are assigned a score of 0, 1, or 2. The provider observes the patient, assigns a score for each criterion, and adds the scores.
